# Popover

A general-purpose floating surface over Radix Popover: focus management, dismiss and collision-aware positioning. Hosts forms, pickers and info cards, with an exposed --surface so nested controls blend in.

```tsx
<Popover>
  <PopoverTrigger asChild>
    <Button variant="outline">Open popover</Button>
  </PopoverTrigger>
  <PopoverContent>
    <div className="space-y-1">
      <PopoverTitle>Invite teammates</PopoverTitle>
      <PopoverDescription>
        Share this workspace with anyone on your team.
      </PopoverDescription>
    </div>
  </PopoverContent>
</Popover>
```

## Installation

```bash
# One-time setup (tokens + lib helpers)
npx koalaui-cli@latest init

# Add this component (its dependencies come along)
npx koalaui-cli@latest add popover
```

Manual: run `npm install radix-ui tailwind-variants tailwind-merge`, then copy the source into `components/ui/popover/` and adjust the import paths to your project. Components pull `cn` from `lib/utils`, the `tv` wrapper from `lib/tv`, and (for multi-part components) `createContext` from `lib/create-context`.

## Usage

```tsx title="usage.tsx"
import {
  Popover,
  PopoverTrigger,
  PopoverContent,
} from "@/components/ui/popover"

export function Example() {
  return (
    <Popover>
      <PopoverTrigger asChild>
        <Button variant="outline">Open</Button>
      </PopoverTrigger>
      <PopoverContent>Content</PopoverContent>
    </Popover>
  )
}
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
import {
  Popover,
  PopoverTrigger,
  PopoverAnchor,
  PopoverContent,
  PopoverViewport,
  PopoverCloseButton,
  PopoverMedia,
  PopoverTitle,
  PopoverDescription,
  PopoverClose,
  PopoverFooter,
} from "@/components/ui/popover"

<Popover>
  <PopoverTrigger />
  <PopoverAnchor />
  <PopoverContent>
    <PopoverCloseButton />
    <PopoverMedia />
    <PopoverTitle />
    <PopoverDescription />
    <PopoverClose />
    <PopoverFooter />
  </PopoverContent>
</Popover>

// One popover, many triggers
<Popover>
  <PopoverTrigger payload={a} />
  <PopoverTrigger payload={b} />
  <PopoverContent>
    <PopoverViewport>{(payload) => …}</PopoverViewport>
  </PopoverContent>
</Popover>
```

## With a form

The canonical use case. Because the content exposes `--surface`, nested `Input`s paint the panel surface rather than the page. Wrap actions in `PopoverClose` to dismiss on click.

```tsx
<Popover>
  <PopoverTrigger asChild>
    <Button variant="outline">Dimensions</Button>
  </PopoverTrigger>
  <PopoverContent className="w-80">
    {/* title + inputs */}
    <PopoverClose asChild>
      <Button size="sm">Save</Button>
    </PopoverClose>
  </PopoverContent>
</Popover>
```

## With arrow & close button

Set `showArrow` for a pointer toward the trigger, and use `PopoverCloseButton` for a styled top-right dismiss.

```tsx
<PopoverContent showArrow className="w-64">
  <PopoverCloseButton aria-label="Close">×</PopoverCloseButton>
  <PopoverTitle>Heads up</PopoverTitle>
  <PopoverDescription>…</PopoverDescription>
</PopoverContent>
```

## Alignment

Control placement along the trigger with `align` (`start` · `center` · `end`) and `side` / `sideOffset`, all forwarded to Radix.

```tsx
<PopoverContent align="start">…</PopoverContent>
<PopoverContent align="center">…</PopoverContent>
<PopoverContent align="end">…</PopoverContent>
```

## Density

`density` tunes the content padding: `compact` for dense application UI. It also cascades from a surrounding `DensityProvider`.

```tsx
<PopoverContent density="compact">…</PopoverContent>
```

## Open on hover

Set `openOnHover` on the trigger (or the root, for every trigger). It opens after `delay` and stays open while the pointer crosses into the panel and rests in it. A click pins it open, and touch and keyboard keep the click behaviour.

```tsx
<Popover>
  <PopoverTrigger asChild openOnHover delay={200}>
    <Button variant="outline">Notifications</Button>
  </PopoverTrigger>
  <PopoverContent className="w-80" density="compact">
    <PopoverTitle>Notifications</PopoverTitle>
    {/* the list */}
  </PopoverContent>
</Popover>
```

Hovering a link to peek at where it goes is a [HoverCard](https://www.koalaui.com/docs/components/hover-card.md): it never takes focus and never opens on touch, so it only previews. A hover Popover is still a dialog. Its trigger is a button, a click or Enter opens it, and it can hold a form.

## Multiple triggers

Any number of triggers can open one popover. Give each a `payload` and pass the content a function of it. One panel serves the whole table, and only the active row's trigger reads as expanded.

```tsx
<Popover>
  <table>
    {members.map((member) => (
      <tr key={member.handle}>
        <td>
          <PopoverTrigger asChild payload={member}>
            <Button variant="ghost" size="sm">{member.name}</Button>
          </PopoverTrigger>
        </td>
        …
      </tr>
    ))}
  </table>
  <PopoverContent side="right" align="start">
    {(member: Member) => <MemberCard member={member} />}
  </PopoverContent>
</Popover>
```

## Detached triggers

Triggers can live outside the `Popover`, in another component. Create a handle once with `createPopoverHandle()` and pass it to the root and to each trigger. The handle also opens and closes the popover from code.

```tsx
const usage = createPopoverHandle<Usage>()

// In the toolbar
<PopoverTrigger handle={usage} payload={seats} id="usage-seats" asChild>
  <Button variant="outline">Seats</Button>
</PopoverTrigger>
<Button onClick={() => usage.open("usage-storage")}>Open storage from code</Button>

// Anywhere else
<Popover handle={usage}>
  <PopoverContent>{(item: Usage) => <UsageCard item={item} />}</PopoverContent>
</Popover>
```

To control it, pass `open` and `triggerId`, and read the new trigger from `onOpenChange`, which also fires on a switch.

```tsx title="controlled.tsx"
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
const [triggerId, setTriggerId] = useState<string | null>(null)

<Popover
  open={open}
  triggerId={triggerId}
  onOpenChange={(next, { triggerId }) => {
    setOpen(next)
    setTriggerId(triggerId)
  }}
>
  …
</Popover>
```

## Animating between triggers

Moving from one trigger to another never closes the panel. It glides to the new trigger, eases to the new size, and the contents slide in the direction it moved. The first open lands in place. Each payload sets its own width, here `w-64` on the card.

```tsx
<Popover openOnHover delay={200}>
  {members.map((member) => (
    <PopoverTrigger key={member.handle} payload={member} aria-label={member.name}>
      <Avatar … />
    </PopoverTrigger>
  ))}
  <PopoverContent>
    {(member: Member) => <MemberCard member={member} />}
  </PopoverContent>
</Popover>
```

A function child renders inside a `PopoverViewport`. Place one yourself to style the switch. Hide the leaving contents for a plain resize, or key off `data-activation-direction`, `data-current` and `data-previous`.

```tsx title="viewport.tsx"
<PopoverContent>
  <PopoverViewport className="[&>[data-previous]]:hidden">
    {(member: Member) => <MemberCard member={member} />}
  </PopoverViewport>
</PopoverContent>
```

## Confirm an action

A lightweight inline confirm for a destructive action. The footer pairs a `ghost` Cancel with a `destructive` primary, each wrapped in `PopoverClose` so either choice dismisses.

```tsx
<Popover>
  <PopoverTrigger asChild>
    <Button variant="outline">Delete project</Button>
  </PopoverTrigger>
  <PopoverContent className="w-72">
    <PopoverTitle>Delete project?</PopoverTitle>
    <PopoverDescription>This permanently removes the project and all of its data.</PopoverDescription>
    <div className="flex justify-end gap-2">
      <PopoverClose asChild><Button variant="ghost" size="sm">Cancel</Button></PopoverClose>
      <PopoverClose asChild><Button variant="destructive" size="sm">Delete</Button></PopoverClose>
    </div>
  </PopoverContent>
</Popover>
```

## Profile card

A richer surface: compose an `Avatar` with identity and actions for a hover-card style preview.

```tsx
<Popover>
  <PopoverTrigger asChild>
    <Button variant="ghost" size="sm">@katiep</Button>
  </PopoverTrigger>
  <PopoverContent className="w-72">
    <div className="flex items-center gap-3">
      <AvatarRoot size="lg">
        <AvatarImage src="https://i.pravatar.cc/160?img=5" alt="Katie Park" />
        <AvatarFallback>KP</AvatarFallback>
        <AvatarStatus variant="online" />
      </AvatarRoot>
      <div className="flex flex-col">
        <span className="text-sm font-semibold text-foreground">Katie Park</span>
        <span className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">@katiep</span>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div className="flex gap-2">
      <Button variant="ghost" size="sm" className="flex-1">Message</Button>
      <Button size="sm" className="flex-1">Follow</Button>
    </div>
  </PopoverContent>
</Popover>
```

## Media and footer

`PopoverMedia` frames a picture or video 8px in from the panel's edges, first or last, with corners concentric to the panel's (16px outside, 8px on the picture). `PopoverFooter` closes the panel with a muted well on the same inset, where a divider line would otherwise go; its text lands back on the copy's line. At `compact` both sit 4px in, with 12px corners.

```tsx
<PopoverContent className="w-80">
  <PopoverMedia>
    <img src="…" alt="A style guide spread" />
  </PopoverMedia>
  <div className="mt-3 flex flex-col gap-1.5">
    <PopoverTitle>Density comes to every form</PopoverTitle>
    <PopoverDescription>One size prop across fields, selects and buttons…</PopoverDescription>
  </div>
  <PopoverFooter className="justify-between">
    <span className="text-muted-foreground">Koala 2.4 · 12 changes</span>
    <Link href="/changelog">Read the notes</Link>
  </PopoverFooter>
</PopoverContent>
```

## Share a link

A read-only `Input` blends with the panel through `--surface`, and the copy button swaps to a confirmation for a beat after a click.

```tsx
const [copied, setCopied] = useState(false)

<PopoverContent className="w-80">
  <PopoverTitle>Share link</PopoverTitle>
  <PopoverDescription>Anyone with this link can view the project.</PopoverDescription>
  <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
    <InputRoot size="sm" className="flex-1">
      <InputField readOnly value="koalaui.com/s/9f3a2" />
    </InputRoot>
    <Button size="sm" className="shrink-0" swapKey={copied ? "copied" : "copy"} onClick={copy}>
      {copied ? "Copied" : "Copy"}
    </Button>
  </div>
</PopoverContent>
```

## Feedback prompt

A common composition: pair the surface with a `ToggleGroup` for a "Was this useful?" rating. The control is its own label, so no inputs are needed. Shown here always visible as a card; the same content drops straight into a `PopoverContent`.

```tsx
<div className="rounded-xl border border-border bg-card p-4 shadow-sm [--surface:var(--card)]">
  <PopoverTitle className="text-base">Was this useful?</PopoverTitle>
  <PopoverDescription>How would you rate your overall experience?</PopoverDescription>
  <ToggleGroup type="single" size="sm" value={rating} onValueChange={setRating}>
    <ToggleGroupItem value="yes"><ThumbsUp />Yes</ToggleGroupItem>
    <ToggleGroupItem value="no"><ThumbsDown />No</ToggleGroupItem>
  </ToggleGroup>
</div>
```

A compact take drops the subtitle and swaps in a thank-you once answered.

```tsx
<div className="rounded-xl border border-border bg-card p-4 shadow-xs [--surface:var(--card)]">
  {answer ? (
    <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">Thanks for your feedback!</p>
  ) : (
    <>
      <p className="text-sm font-semibold">Was this useful?</p>
      <ToggleGroup type="single" size="sm" value={answer} onValueChange={setAnswer}>
        <ToggleGroupItem value="yes"><ThumbsUp />Yes</ToggleGroupItem>
        <ToggleGroupItem value="no"><ThumbsDown />No</ToggleGroupItem>
      </ToggleGroup>
    </>
  )}
</div>
```

And floated in the popover itself, revealed from a trigger.

```tsx
<Popover>
  <PopoverTrigger asChild>
    <Button variant="outline">Was this useful?</Button>
  </PopoverTrigger>
  <PopoverContent align="start" className="w-auto">
    <PopoverTitle className="text-base">Was this useful?</PopoverTitle>
    <PopoverDescription>How would you rate your overall experience?</PopoverDescription>
    <ToggleGroup type="single" size="sm" value={rating} onValueChange={setRating}>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="yes"><ThumbsUp />Yes</ToggleGroupItem>
      <ToggleGroupItem value="no"><ThumbsDown />No</ToggleGroupItem>
    </ToggleGroup>
  </PopoverContent>
</Popover>
```

## API reference

### Popover

The root. Owns the open state and the active trigger. Renders no element.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| open | boolean | - | The open state, controlled. |
| defaultOpen | boolean | false | The open state on first render, uncontrolled. |
| onOpenChange | (open: boolean, details: PopoverOpenChangeDetails) => void | - | Fires on open, on close, and on a switch between triggers (still `true`). `details` carries `reason`, `triggerId` and `trigger`. |
| triggerId | string \| null | - | The active trigger, controlled. Pair with `details.triggerId`. |
| defaultTriggerId | string \| null | null | The active trigger on first render. Without one, the first trigger anchors the panel. |
| handle | PopoverHandle | - | Links triggers rendered outside this root. From `createPopoverHandle()`. |
| openOnHover | boolean | false | Open every trigger on hover. A trigger's own prop wins. |
| delay | number | 300 | Milliseconds of hover before it opens. |
| closeDelay | number | 150 | Milliseconds before it closes once the pointer leaves the trigger or the panel. Enough to cross the gap. |
| modal | boolean | false | Trap focus in the panel and block the page behind it. |

### PopoverTrigger

A button that opens the popover. Any number of them can open one popover.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| asChild | boolean | false | Render the child element as the trigger, merging props onto it. |
| payload | unknown | - | Handed to the content's render function while this trigger is active. |
| handle | PopoverHandle | - | Links a trigger outside its `Popover`. |
| id | string | - | Names the trigger for `triggerId` and `handle.open(id)`. Also its DOM id. |
| openOnHover | boolean | - | Open on hover. Inherits the root's. |
| delay | number | - | Hover delay for this trigger. Inherits the root's. |
| closeDelay | number | - | Close delay for this trigger. Inherits the root's. |

| Data attribute | Description |
| --- | --- |
| data-state | `open` on the active trigger while the panel is open, else `closed`. |
| data-popover-trigger | The trigger's id. `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` follow the active trigger only. |

### PopoverContent

The floating panel, portalled to the body. Forwards every Radix `Popover.Content` prop.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | ReactNode \| (payload) => ReactNode | - | The contents, or a function of the active payload. A function renders in a `PopoverViewport`. |
| side | "top" \| "right" \| "bottom" \| "left" | "bottom" | The preferred side of the trigger. Flips on collision. |
| sideOffset | number | 8 | The gap to the trigger, in pixels. |
| align | "start" \| "center" \| "end" | "center" | Alignment along the trigger. |
| collisionPadding | number | 8 | The room kept from the viewport edge. |
| density | "comfortable" \| "compact" | "comfortable" | The padding: 16px or 12px. Inherits from a `DensityProvider`. |
| showArrow | boolean | false | Render a small pointer toward the trigger. |

| Data attribute | Description |
| --- | --- |
| data-state | `open` or `closed`. |
| data-side | The side it was placed on, after collisions. |
| data-align | The alignment it was placed with. |

| CSS variable | Description |
| --- | --- |
| --surface | The panel colour, read by nested controls so they blend with it. |
| --popover-padding | The density padding, which the viewport moves onto its contents. |
| --popover-inset-radius | The corner of inset media and footer, concentric with the panel. |
| --radix-popover-content-transform-origin | The trigger side the panel grows from. |

### PopoverViewport

The box the contents switch in. Eases to each payload's size and slides the contents in the direction the panel moved.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | ReactNode \| (payload) => ReactNode | - | The contents, or a function of the active payload. |

| Data attribute | Description |
| --- | --- |
| data-activation-direction | Where the new trigger sits from the old: `left`, `right`, `up` or `down`. |
| data-instant | Set until the first switch, so the first open lands at its size. |
| data-current | On the arriving contents. |
| data-previous | On the leaving contents, until their exit ends. |

### createPopoverHandle

Creates a handle shared by a root and its detached triggers. Call it once, outside render. Returns `open(triggerId?)`, `close()` and `isOpen`.

### PopoverAnchor

Anchors the panel to another element, such as a field around the trigger. Replaces the trigger anchor.

### PopoverClose

Closes the popover on click. Use `asChild` to keep your own button.

### PopoverCloseButton

A styled close button pinned to the top-right corner. Pass your icon as the child.

### PopoverTitle

The panel's heading, an `h4`.

### PopoverDescription

Muted supporting copy under the title.

### PopoverMedia

A picture or video set in from the panel's edges, with concentric corners. First or last.

### PopoverFooter

A muted well that closes the panel, inset like the media. Always last.

## FAQ

### When should I use a Popover instead of a DropdownMenu or Tooltip?

Reach for Popover to host arbitrary content like forms, pickers, or info cards. DropdownMenu is for lists of actions with menu keyboard semantics, and Tooltip is for a passive hover hint.

### How do I dismiss the popover when a button inside it is clicked?

Wrap the control in `PopoverClose` (use `asChild` to keep your own Button styling), and it closes the panel on click with no extra wiring. `PopoverCloseButton` is a ready-made styled top-right dismiss.

### Why do Inputs inside PopoverContent blend with the panel instead of the page?

PopoverContent exposes `--surface: var(--popover)`, so nested controls like Input and Select read that variable and paint the panel surface rather than a separate background block.

### How do I position the panel and add a pointer to the trigger?

Pass `align` (start, center, end), `side`, and `sideOffset`, all forwarded to Radix with collision-aware repositioning. Set `showArrow` to render a small arrow pointing at the trigger.

### How does density affect the popover?

The `density` prop tunes the content padding: `comfortable` is `p-4` and `compact` is `p-3`, and with it how far `PopoverMedia` and `PopoverFooter` sit in from the edge (8px or 4px, with the matching concentric radius). It also cascades from a surrounding DensityProvider.

### Should I use openOnHover or a HoverCard?

A HoverCard previews where a link goes: it never takes focus and never opens on touch. Use `openOnHover` when the panel is still a dialog you can reach by click or keyboard, like a notifications list or a row's details.

### How do several triggers share one popover?

Render them all inside one `Popover`, or pass the same `createPopoverHandle()` handle to the root and to triggers elsewhere. Each trigger carries a `payload`, and the content can be a function of it. Switching triggers keeps the panel open and glides it to the new one.

### Do I need the helper parts like PopoverTitle and PopoverDescription?

No, they are optional structured-content helpers for consistent typography. PopoverContent will host any children you give it.

## Exports and dependencies

`npx koalaui-cli@latest add popover` writes `components/ui/popover/`. Import from `@/components/ui/popover`:

- Components and helpers: `Popover`, `PopoverTrigger`, `PopoverAnchor`, `PopoverClose`, `PopoverContent`, `PopoverViewport`, `PopoverTitle`, `PopoverDescription`, `PopoverMedia`, `PopoverFooter`, `PopoverCloseButton`, `createPopoverHandle`, `popoverVariants`
- Types: `PopoverProps`, `PopoverTriggerProps`, `PopoverContentProps`, `PopoverViewportProps`, `PopoverHandle`, `PopoverOpenChangeDetails`, `PopoverOpenChangeReason`
- Koala lib helpers it uses: `density`, `tv`
- npm packages: `radix-ui`
